headline: OpenAI confirmed it fired three safety researchers accused of passing confidential information to outside AI safety groups.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the firings were reported on 1 Oct and already in the 2 Oct pool; today's article adds no new fact.
importance_line: Outside auditors who the public relies on to check AI labs may now get less cooperation from staff inside them, and OpenAI must show that policing leaks does not mean shutting out independent safety review; the three researchers have not given their side.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on 1 Oct 2026, as relayed by The Times of India, that OpenAI dismissed safety researchers Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni for allegedly sharing confidential information with outside AI safety organisations, and OpenAI confirmed that the three "mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures". Korbak had been OpenAI's contact for the non-profits METR and Redwood Research during their investigation of the Hugging Face agent breach, and the firings land in the same week OpenAI shelved its GPT-6.1 Astra launch over safety concerns.
notes: Follow-up of 2 Oct item C12-03; nothing new today beyond a recap. Source is the WSJ (the original reporter); url is the Times of India page where the text was read because the WSJ link was not given. Below the 5 cutoff.
